q21826.en: The panel shown indicates that a tight bend is near.

explain.short: It marks a hairpin, which is a very tight bend, so a tight bend is close.
explain.rule: The white square panel '1° tornante' (1st hairpin bend) marks the first of a series of hairpins (very tight bends). The number is progressive: the next panels say 2°, 3° and so on.
explain.trap: 'curva stretta' (tight bend) is just another way to say 'tornante'.

sceneParams.caption: 1st hairpin: a tight bend is here

q21827.en: The panel shown indicates the progressive number of a dangerous bend.

explain.short: The '1°' is the progressive number: this is the first hairpin, a dangerous bend.
explain.rule: The white square panel '1° tornante' (1st hairpin bend) marks the first of a series of hairpins (very tight bends). The number is progressive: the next panels say 2°, 3° and so on.
explain.trap: 'numero progressivo' (running number) is exactly what '1°' shows.

sceneParams.caption: '1°' = number of the bend in the series

q21828.en: The panel shown indicates the first of a series of hairpin bends (bends with a small radius).

explain.short: '1° tornante' means 'first hairpin': more hairpins follow.
explain.rule: The white square panel '1° tornante' (1st hairpin bend) marks the first of a series of hairpins (very tight bends). The number is progressive: the next panels say 2°, 3° and so on.
explain.trap: 'il primo' (the first) matches the '1°' on the panel.

q21829.en: In a series of hairpin bends, the panel shown indicates its progressive number.

explain.short: Each hairpin in the series has its own panel with its number: 1°, 2°, 3°...
explain.rule: The white square panel '1° tornante' (1st hairpin bend) marks the first of a series of hairpins (very tight bends). The number is progressive: the next panels say 2°, 3° and so on.
explain.trap: 'ne indica il numero progressivo' means it shows the hairpin's running number.

q21830.en: The panel shown indicates an area with roundabout traffic.

explain.short: It marks a hairpin bend, not a roundabout.
explain.rule: The white square panel '1° tornante' (1st hairpin bend) marks the first of a series of hairpins (very tight bends). The number is progressive: the next panels say 2°, 3° and so on.
explain.trap: 'circolazione rotatoria' (roundabout) has a blue round sign with three arrows, not this panel.

q21831.en: The panel shown indicates that we will find a hairpin bend in one kilometre.

explain.short: '1°' is the hairpin's number in the series, not a distance in km.
explain.rule: The white square panel '1° tornante' (1st hairpin bend) marks the first of a series of hairpins (very tight bends). The number is progressive: the next panels say 2°, 3° and so on.
explain.trap: 'fra un chilometro' (in one km): the panel shows no 'km'; '1°' means 'first'.

q21832.en: The panel shown indicates the kilometres to drive before you can turn back.

explain.short: It does not talk about turning back: it numbers the hairpin bends.
explain.rule: The white square panel '1° tornante' (1st hairpin bend) marks the first of a series of hairpins (very tight bends). The number is progressive: the next panels say 2°, 3° and so on.
explain.trap: 'tornare indietro' (turn back) sounds like 'tornante', but they are different words.

sceneParams.caption: Hairpin number, not km to turn back

q21833.en: The panel shown indicates the number of junctions passed.

explain.short: It counts hairpin bends, not junctions.
explain.rule: The white square panel '1° tornante' (1st hairpin bend) marks the first of a series of hairpins (very tight bends). The number is progressive: the next panels say 2°, 3° and so on.
explain.trap: 'incroci' (junctions) is wrong: the word on the panel is 'tornante'.

q21834.en: The panel shown indicates how many kilometres away the next hairpin bend is.

explain.short: '1°' means first hairpin; it is not a distance.
explain.rule: The white square panel '1° tornante' (1st hairpin bend) marks the first of a series of hairpins (very tight bends). The number is progressive: the next panels say 2°, 3° and so on.
explain.trap: 'a quanti chilometri' (how many km away): no distance is shown.

q21835.en: The panel shown indicates the number of the overpass.

explain.short: It numbers hairpin bends, not overpasses (bridges over the road).
explain.rule: The white square panel '1° tornante' (1st hairpin bend) marks the first of a series of hairpins (very tight bends). The number is progressive: the next panels say 2°, 3° and so on.
explain.trap: 'cavalcavia' (overpass) has nothing to do with 'tornante'.

q21836.en: The sign shown indicates the recommended direction for lorries with a maximum laden mass over 3.5 tonnes.

explain.short: The lorry symbol and the arrow show which way heavy lorries are advised to go.
explain.rule: The YELLOW panel with an arrow and a lorry is a temporary roadworks sign. At a junction before roadworks, it shows the recommended direction for lorries over 3.5 tonnes. It advises, it does not order.
explain.trap: 'consigliata' (recommended): it is advice, not an obligation.

sceneParams.caption: Lorries over 3.5 t: advised to go right

q21837.en: The sign shown indicates the category of vehicles to which the turn is recommended.

explain.short: The lorry symbol tells you which vehicles the advised turn is for.
explain.rule: The YELLOW panel with an arrow and a lorry is a temporary roadworks sign. At a junction before roadworks, it shows the recommended direction for lorries over 3.5 tonnes. It advises, it does not order.
explain.trap: 'categoria di veicoli' (category of vehicles) is shown by the lorry drawing.

sceneParams.caption: The lorry = who the advice is for

q21838.en: The sign shown is placed at the point of the recommended detour for lorries over 3.5 tonnes.

explain.short: It stands right where the lorries should turn off.
explain.rule: The YELLOW panel with an arrow and a lorry is a temporary roadworks sign. At a junction before roadworks, it shows the recommended direction for lorries over 3.5 tonnes. It advises, it does not order.
explain.trap: 'nel punto della deviazione' (at the point of the detour): it is at the turn itself.

q21839.en: The sign shown may be preceded by an advance-warning sign.

explain.short: Before the turn there may be a sign announcing it earlier, so lorry drivers can get ready.
explain.rule: The YELLOW panel with an arrow and a lorry is a temporary roadworks sign. At a junction before roadworks, it shows the recommended direction for lorries over 3.5 tonnes. It advises, it does not order.
explain.trap: 'può' (may): an advance warning is possible, not always present.

sceneParams.caption: May have an advance warning before it

q21840.en: The sign shown is found near a junction that comes before a roadworks site.

explain.short: The yellow colour means roadworks: lorries are sent off the road before the works.
explain.rule: The YELLOW panel with an arrow and a lorry is a temporary roadworks sign. At a junction before roadworks, it shows the recommended direction for lorries over 3.5 tonnes. It advises, it does not order.
explain.trap: Yellow background = 'cantiere stradale' (roadworks site) nearby.

q21841.en: The sign shown indicates that turning left is forbidden.

explain.short: It only advises lorries to go right; it forbids nothing.
explain.rule: The YELLOW panel with an arrow and a lorry is a temporary roadworks sign. At a junction before roadworks, it shows the recommended direction for lorries over 3.5 tonnes. It advises, it does not order.
explain.trap: 'vietato' (forbidden): this sign gives advice, not a ban.

sceneParams.caption: Advice for lorries, not a ban

q21842.en: The sign shown indicates a parking area for lorries.

explain.short: It shows a direction for lorries, not a place to park.
explain.rule: The YELLOW panel with an arrow and a lorry is a temporary roadworks sign. At a junction before roadworks, it shows the recommended direction for lorries over 3.5 tonnes. It advises, it does not order.
explain.trap: 'area di sosta' (parking area) would be a blue 'P' sign.

q21843.en: The sign shown indicates the direction to follow to reach a landfill (dump).

explain.short: It is the advised route for heavy lorries because of roadworks, not a way to a dump.
explain.rule: The YELLOW panel with an arrow and a lorry is a temporary roadworks sign. At a junction before roadworks, it shows the recommended direction for lorries over 3.5 tonnes. It advises, it does not order.
explain.trap: 'discarica' (landfill) is not on the sign: the lorry is about heavy vehicles.

sceneParams.caption: Lorry route, not the way to a dump

q21844.en: The sign shown indicates a one-way road on the right, reserved only for lorries.

explain.short: It is not a one-way sign and the road is not reserved: lorries are only advised to go there.
explain.rule: The YELLOW panel with an arrow and a lorry is a temporary roadworks sign. At a junction before roadworks, it shows the recommended direction for lorries over 3.5 tonnes. It advises, it does not order.
explain.trap: 'senso unico' and 'riservata solo' (one-way, reserved only) are both wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Advised route, not one-way or reserved

q21845.en: The sign shown obliges lorries to turn right.

explain.short: It recommends the right turn; it does not order it.
explain.rule: The YELLOW panel with an arrow and a lorry is a temporary roadworks sign. At a junction before roadworks, it shows the recommended direction for lorries over 3.5 tonnes. It advises, it does not order.
explain.trap: 'obbliga' (obliges) is wrong: the direction is only recommended.

q21846.en: The sign shown gives advance warning of works in progress.

explain.short: The digging worker on a yellow background means roadworks ahead.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a YELLOW background and a digging worker means roadworks ('lavori'). It warns of work sites, materials or machines on the road and workers on or near the carriageway (the part of the road for vehicles).
explain.trap: 'preavvisa' (warns in advance): the works are just ahead.

q21847.en: The sign shown gives advance warning of work sites.

explain.short: A work site ('cantiere') is exactly what this sign announces.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a YELLOW background and a digging worker means roadworks ('lavori'). It warns of work sites, materials or machines on the road and workers on or near the carriageway (the part of the road for vehicles).
explain.trap: 'cantieri di lavoro' (work sites) means roadworks.

q21848.en: The sign shown gives advance warning of any temporary storage of materials or machinery.

explain.short: Roadworks can leave materials or machines on the road; this sign covers that too.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a YELLOW background and a digging worker means roadworks ('lavori'). It warns of work sites, materials or machines on the road and workers on or near the carriageway (the part of the road for vehicles).
explain.trap: 'eventuali depositi temporanei' (possible temporary storage) is part of the works.

sceneParams.caption: Materials or machines may be on the road

q21849.en: The sign shown gives advance warning of the possible presence of people working near or on the carriageway.

explain.short: Workers may be on or beside the road, so slow down and watch out.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a YELLOW background and a digging worker means roadworks ('lavori'). It warns of work sites, materials or machines on the road and workers on or near the carriageway (the part of the road for vehicles).
explain.trap: 'uomini che lavorano' (people working) is exactly the drawing.

sceneParams.caption: Workers may be on the road

q21850.en: The sign shown can be completed by a panel showing the length of the work site.

explain.short: An extra panel under it can say how long the stretch of works is.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a YELLOW background and a digging worker means roadworks ('lavori'). It warns of work sites, materials or machines on the road and workers on or near the carriageway (the part of the road for vehicles).
explain.trap: 'può essere integrato' (can be completed) means an extra panel is possible.

sceneParams.caption: Extra panel may give the works length

q21851.en: The sign shown requires you to give way to vehicles leaving the work site.

explain.short: It only warns of roadworks; it gives no priority rule.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a YELLOW background and a digging worker means roadworks ('lavori'). It warns of work sites, materials or machines on the road and workers on or near the carriageway (the part of the road for vehicles).
explain.trap: 'impone di dare la precedenza' (requires giving way): a danger sign warns, it gives no orders.

q21852.en: The sign shown warns that you must give way to vehicles coming from the opposite direction.

explain.short: That is a different sign (narrow passage, red and black arrows). This one only warns of roadworks.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a YELLOW background and a digging worker means roadworks ('lavori'). It warns of work sites, materials or machines on the road and workers on or near the carriageway (the part of the road for vehicles).
explain.trap: 'senso opposto' (opposite direction): giving way to oncoming traffic has its own sign.

sceneParams.caption: Roadworks, not give way to oncoming

q21853.en: The sign shown obliges you to turn back during the workers' working hours.

explain.short: It never tells you to turn around; you pass the works carefully.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a YELLOW background and a digging worker means roadworks ('lavori'). It warns of work sites, materials or machines on the road and workers on or near the carriageway (the part of the road for vehicles).
explain.trap: 'invertire il senso di marcia' (turn back, U-turn) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: No U-turn order: just slow down

q21854.en: The sign shown obliges you to give way to the road workers.

explain.short: It warns that workers may be there, so you take care; it gives no give-way order.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a YELLOW background and a digging worker means roadworks ('lavori'). It warns of work sites, materials or machines on the road and workers on or near the carriageway (the part of the road for vehicles).
explain.trap: 'obbliga a dare la precedenza' (obliges you to give way): a danger sign creates no priority.

sceneParams.caption: Be careful, but no give-way order

q21855.en: The sign shown warns of alternating one-way traffic.

explain.short: Alternating one-way traffic has its own signs (often traffic lights). This one only warns of roadworks.
explain.rule: The red triangle with a YELLOW background and a digging worker means roadworks ('lavori'). It warns of work sites, materials or machines on the road and workers on or near the carriageway (the part of the road for vehicles).
explain.trap: 'senso unico alternato' (alternating one-way) is a different sign.

q21856.en: The barrier shown marks an area occupied by a roadworks site.

explain.short: Red and white striped barriers close off roadworks areas.
explain.rule: A bar with diagonal RED and WHITE stripes on two posts is a roadworks barrier. It closes off and marks the edges of a works area; it can also replace broken level-crossing gates.
explain.trap: 'area occupata da un cantiere' (area occupied by a work site) is the works zone.

q21857.en: The barrier shown marks off an area where roadworks are being carried out.

explain.short: It delimits (marks the edge of) the zone where work is going on.
explain.rule: A bar with diagonal RED and WHITE stripes on two posts is a roadworks barrier. It closes off and marks the edges of a works area; it can also replace broken level-crossing gates.
explain.trap: 'delimita' (marks off) is exactly what a barrier does.

q21858.en: The barrier shown is placed at the edges of a roadworks site.

explain.short: Barriers stand along the edges of the work site to keep traffic out.
explain.rule: A bar with diagonal RED and WHITE stripes on two posts is a roadworks barrier. It closes off and marks the edges of a works area; it can also replace broken level-crossing gates.
explain.trap: 'ai bordi' (at the edges) is where barriers go.

sceneParams.caption: Placed at the edges of the works

q21859.en: The barrier shown can be used at level crossings when the gates are broken.

explain.short: If a level crossing's gates are out of order, this barrier can close the road instead.
explain.rule: A bar with diagonal RED and WHITE stripes on two posts is a roadworks barrier. It closes off and marks the edges of a works area; it can also replace broken level-crossing gates.
explain.trap: 'sbarre guaste' (broken gates): the barrier replaces them.

sceneParams.caption: Also at level crossings with broken gates

q21860.en: The barrier shown can be completed by a lantern with a steady red light in case of poor visibility.

explain.short: At night or in fog a steady red light helps drivers see the barrier.
explain.rule: A bar with diagonal RED and WHITE stripes on two posts is a roadworks barrier. It closes off and marks the edges of a works area; it can also replace broken level-crossing gates.
explain.trap: 'luce rossa fissa' means a red light that stays on and does not flash.

sceneParams.caption: Steady red lantern in poor visibility

keywords.en: lantern with a steady red light

q21861.en: The barrier shown is found at the entrance of a garage.

explain.short: It is a roadworks barrier, not a garage gate.
explain.rule: A bar with diagonal RED and WHITE stripes on two posts is a roadworks barrier. It closes off and marks the edges of a works area; it can also replace broken level-crossing gates.
explain.trap: 'autorimessa' (garage) has nothing to do with roadworks.

q21862.en: The barrier shown marks a car park reserved for roadworks vehicles.

explain.short: It closes off a works area; it does not mark parking.
explain.rule: A bar with diagonal RED and WHITE stripes on two posts is a roadworks barrier. It closes off and marks the edges of a works area; it can also replace broken level-crossing gates.
explain.trap: 'parcheggio riservato' (reserved car park) is wrong.

q21863.en: The barrier shown is found at motorway toll booths to separate the lanes.

explain.short: It is used for roadworks, not to divide toll lanes.
explain.rule: A bar with diagonal RED and WHITE stripes on two posts is a roadworks barrier. It closes off and marks the edges of a works area; it can also replace broken level-crossing gates.
explain.trap: 'caselli autostradali' (motorway toll booths) is wrong.

q21864.en: The barrier shown signals a dangerous bend.

explain.short: A dangerous bend has its own red triangle sign; this barrier closes off roadworks.
explain.rule: A bar with diagonal RED and WHITE stripes on two posts is a roadworks barrier. It closes off and marks the edges of a works area; it can also replace broken level-crossing gates.
explain.trap: 'curva pericolosa' (dangerous bend) is a different sign.

q21865.en: The barriers signal a cycle route.

explain.short: They close off roadworks; a cycle path has a blue round sign with a bicycle.
explain.rule: A bar with diagonal RED and WHITE stripes on two posts is a roadworks barrier. It closes off and marks the edges of a works area; it can also replace broken level-crossing gates.
explain.trap: 'percorso ciclabile' (cycle route) has nothing to do with roadworks.

q21866.en: The cone shown can mark off short-term work zones.

explain.short: Cones are quick to put down and remove, so they suit short works.
explain.rule: The cone with RED and WHITE bands is for short-lasting, temporary situations: short works, temporary detours, accident areas, a temporary split of the two directions. Longer works use other, sturdier devices.
explain.trap: 'di breve durata' (short-term) is the key: cones are for short works.

q21867.en: The cone shown can be used to mark temporary detours.

explain.short: A line of cones can guide traffic along a temporary detour.
explain.rule: The cone with RED and WHITE bands is for short-lasting, temporary situations: short works, temporary detours, accident areas, a temporary split of the two directions. Longer works use other, sturdier devices.
explain.trap: 'deviazioni provvisorie' (temporary detours) are temporary, like cones.

q21868.en: The cone shown can be used to mark areas affected by accidents.

explain.short: Police and rescue teams use cones to close off an accident area quickly.
explain.rule: The cone with RED and WHITE bands is for short-lasting, temporary situations: short works, temporary detours, accident areas, a temporary split of the two directions. Longer works use other, sturdier devices.
explain.trap: 'aree interessate da incidenti' (accident areas): a quick, temporary use.

q21869.en: The cone shown can indicate a temporary separation of the directions of travel.

explain.short: A row of cones can split the two directions of traffic for a while.
explain.rule: The cone with RED and WHITE bands is for short-lasting, temporary situations: short works, temporary detours, accident areas, a temporary split of the two directions. Longer works use other, sturdier devices.
explain.trap: 'separazione provvisoria' (temporary separation): temporary again.

sceneParams.caption: Cones can split the two directions

q21870.en: The cone shown is used to indicate a reserved parking space.

explain.short: Road cones are for works and temporary hazards, not to reserve parking.
explain.rule: The cone with RED and WHITE bands is for short-lasting, temporary situations: short works, temporary detours, accident areas, a temporary split of the two directions. Longer works use other, sturdier devices.
explain.trap: 'parcheggio riservato' (reserved parking) is not a use of this cone.

sceneParams.caption: Works and hazards, not reserved parking

q21871.en: The cone shown can be used for roadworks lasting more than 10 days.

explain.short: Cones are for short works; long works need sturdier, more lasting devices.
explain.rule: The cone with RED and WHITE bands is for short-lasting, temporary situations: short works, temporary detours, accident areas, a temporary split of the two directions. Longer works use other, sturdier devices.
explain.trap: 'superiori a 10 giorni' (more than 10 days) is too long for cones.

q21872.en: The cone shown is used on roads where heavy snowfall occurs.

explain.short: Cones are for works and temporary hazards; they have nothing to do with snow.
explain.rule: The cone with RED and WHITE bands is for short-lasting, temporary situations: short works, temporary detours, accident areas, a temporary split of the two directions. Longer works use other, sturdier devices.
explain.trap: 'abbondanti nevicate' (heavy snowfall) is not a use of cones.

q21873.en: The cone shown separates the carriageway from the cycle path.

explain.short: A cycle path is separated by kerbs or road markings, not by cones.
explain.rule: The cone with RED and WHITE bands is for short-lasting, temporary situations: short works, temporary detours, accident areas, a temporary split of the two directions. Longer works use other, sturdier devices.
explain.trap: 'pista ciclabile' (cycle path) is permanent; cones are temporary.

q21874.en: The cone shown indicates an obstacle located outside the carriageway.

explain.short: Cones stand on the road itself, where works or hazards affect traffic.
explain.rule: The cone with RED and WHITE bands is for short-lasting, temporary situations: short works, temporary detours, accident areas, a temporary split of the two directions. Longer works use other, sturdier devices.
explain.trap: 'fuori della carreggiata' (outside the carriageway) is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: On the road, not off it

q21875.en: The sign shown can be placed on roadworks vehicles that are stopped or moving slowly.

explain.short: This panel is mounted on works vehicles to show drivers how to get past them.
explain.rule: This RED and WHITE striped panel with a blue disc and a white arrow pointing down-RIGHT is mounted on works vehicles that are stopped or moving slowly. Slow down and pass the vehicle on the RIGHT.
explain.trap: 'fermi o in lento movimento' (stopped or moving slowly): both cases count.

sceneParams.caption: Works vehicle: pass on the right

q21876.en: The sign shown indicates the side on which the vehicle carrying it must be passed.

explain.short: The arrow points down to the right: pass the vehicle on its right side.
explain.rule: This RED and WHITE striped panel with a blue disc and a white arrow pointing down-RIGHT is mounted on works vehicles that are stopped or moving slowly. Slow down and pass the vehicle on the RIGHT.
explain.trap: 'il lato' (the side) is shown by the arrow.

sceneParams.caption: Arrow shows the side: pass on the right

q21877.en: The sign shown can be placed on road-maintenance vehicles parked on the carriageway.

explain.short: A maintenance vehicle stopped on the road carries this panel to show where to pass.
explain.rule: This RED and WHITE striped panel with a blue disc and a white arrow pointing down-RIGHT is mounted on works vehicles that are stopped or moving slowly. Slow down and pass the vehicle on the RIGHT.
explain.trap: 'in sosta sulla carreggiata' (parked on the carriageway) is one of its uses.

q21878.en: The sign shown can be placed on some roadworks vehicles travelling at low speed.

explain.short: Slow works vehicles, for example line-painting trucks, can carry it too.
explain.rule: This RED and WHITE striped panel with a blue disc and a white arrow pointing down-RIGHT is mounted on works vehicles that are stopped or moving slowly. Slow down and pass the vehicle on the RIGHT.
explain.trap: 'procedono a bassa velocità' (travel at low speed): moving vehicles count too.

q21879.en: The sign shown invites drivers to reduce speed because vehicles may be stopped or moving slowly.

explain.short: When you see it, a works vehicle ahead is stopped or slow: slow down.
explain.rule: This RED and WHITE striped panel with a blue disc and a white arrow pointing down-RIGHT is mounted on works vehicles that are stopped or moving slowly. Slow down and pass the vehicle on the RIGHT.
explain.trap: 'diminuire la velocità' (reduce speed) is right: slow down before passing.

sceneParams.caption: Slow down, then pass on the right

q21880.en: The sign shown indicates that you pass the obstacle on the left.

explain.short: The arrow points down to the RIGHT: you pass on the right, not the left.
explain.rule: This RED and WHITE striped panel with a blue disc and a white arrow pointing down-RIGHT is mounted on works vehicles that are stopped or moving slowly. Slow down and pass the vehicle on the RIGHT.
explain.trap: 'sulla sinistra' (on the left) is the opposite of the arrow.

sceneParams.caption: Arrow points right: pass on the right

q21881.en: The sign shown indicates that you must turn right immediately.

explain.short: It tells you which side to pass the vehicle on; it is not a turn.
explain.rule: This RED and WHITE striped panel with a blue disc and a white arrow pointing down-RIGHT is mounted on works vehicles that are stopped or moving slowly. Slow down and pass the vehicle on the RIGHT.
explain.trap: 'svoltare' (turn) is wrong: the arrow pointing down means 'pass on this side'.

sceneParams.caption: Pass on the right, not turn right

q21882.en: The sign shown indicates the right lane closed for road maintenance.

explain.short: It tells you to pass on the right of the vehicle, so the right side is open, not closed.
explain.rule: This RED and WHITE striped panel with a blue disc and a white arrow pointing down-RIGHT is mounted on works vehicles that are stopped or moving slowly. Slow down and pass the vehicle on the RIGHT.
explain.trap: 'corsia di destra chiusa' (right lane closed) is the opposite: you pass on the right.

q21883.en: The sign shown obliges you to park on the right.

explain.short: It tells you to pass the vehicle on the right, not to stop there.
explain.rule: This RED and WHITE striped panel with a blue disc and a white arrow pointing down-RIGHT is mounted on works vehicles that are stopped or moving slowly. Slow down and pass the vehicle on the RIGHT.
explain.trap: 'sostare' (park, stay stopped) is wrong: you keep moving, slowly.

sceneParams.caption: Pass on the right, don't park
